CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual visit

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
27-year-old female presenting for annual examination. Patient reports struggling with depression, worsened by prolonged indoor and remote work over the past year. She is currently on Prozac 20 mg daily and reports it has helped in the past. She feels that increasing the dose may help her through this difficult period. Patient also reports chronic back pain, particularly exacerbated by prolonged sitting at her desk at work. Pain improves with movement and standing. She denies pain radiating down her legs but reports some numbness in the lower extremities that feels like "falling asleep." Symptoms improve with position changes. She denies leg weakness. Patient is able to perform activities of daily living, though symptoms worsen with prolonged standing or sitting. She reports history of congenital artery requiring coronary artery bypass grafting at a young age. Heart has been doing well with stable appearing arteries.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies weakness in legs. Denies tingling or pain radiating down legs. Reports some numbness in lower extremities. Denies any other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Chronic back pain
Congenital coronary artery anomaly s/p coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in childhood

MEDICATIONS
Prozac 20 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works remotely; reports prolonged time at desk

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears well, no acute distress
Neck: No thyroid enlargement
Cardiovascular: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally
Abdomen: Soft
Musculoskeletal: Pain with palpation of lumbar spine, decreased flexion of back, lower extremity strength intact, no edema

RESULTS
ECG: Basically unchanged from prior year
Lumbar spine X-ray: Stable from prior year

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Increase Prozac from 20 mg to 40 mg daily (one tablet once daily). Patient agrees to medication adjustment.
2. Chronic back pain: Refer to physical therapy for symptom management. Patient declines pain medication at this time, preferring to start with physical therapy.
3. History of CABG s/p congenital coronary artery anomaly: Continue aspirin 81 mg daily. Order echocardiogram for follow-up surveillance.
